newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK exports seen up as global demand revives-report.
newsitem.headline: HK exports seen up as global demand revives-report.

text.p: Hong Kong's export performance should improve as global demand improves, Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp said in a report on Friday.
Hong Kong's recent uninspiring external trade performance has raised concern over possible consequences for the territory's future economic growth, the bank noted.
A protracted slump in exports coupled with moderation in its provision of trade-related services could detract from the territory's promsing economic recovery, it said.

Hongkong Bank said that apart from the disruption of trade flows by some one-off factors in earlier this year, such as the severe U.S. winter and Sino-Taiwan tensions, the slow-down in exports primarily reflects a general downturn in global demand.
With a gradual improvement in overseas demand on the horizon, however, the short-term prospects for Hong Kong's external trade remain promising, it siad.

Recent changes in China's trade and investment policies, such as a cut in the value-added tax rebate on exports, could have important implications for Hong Kong's exports -- with growth in trade related to outward processing activity expected to slow in the longer term, the bank said.
But China's rapidly expanding trade will provide strong support to Hong Kong's external sector, it said.
